## Add LazyClassKey annotation for lazy class-keyed map injection

Implement a new `@LazyClassKey` annotation that allows Dagger to inject maps keyed by Class objects without eagerly loading the Class when the map value isn't needed. This annotation should be used on `@MapKey`-annotated methods to indicate that the map key should be represented as a lazy reference, deferring class loading until the value is actually accessed.

    The implementation requires changes to the generated code infrastructure:
    1. Support for generating anonymous `Lazy` implementations in code blocks
    2. Addition of `MapBuilder` type reference
    3. Refactoring `MapRequestRepresentation` to separate the underlying map expression generation from the dependency expression
    4. Allow `MapFactoryCreationExpression` to work with `Object` as a generic type parameter instead of requiring specific value types

    This change is part of optimizing Dagger's generated code to avoid unnecessary class loading in scenarios where maps with Class keys are injected but not all values are accessed.

## Environment Setup
Check the following configuration files for build and test setup:
    - `BUILD` - Bazel build configuration
    - `WORKSPACE` - Bazel workspace configuration
    - `.bazelrc` - Bazel settings
    - `build_defs.bzl` - Build definitions
    - `test_defs.bzl` - Test definitions
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - CI workflow configuration

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `anonymousLazy` static method to `CodeBlocks.java` that generates an anonymous `Lazy` implementation with a `get()` method containing the provided body code.
    2. Add `MAP_BUILDER` and `STRING` constant references to `TypeNames.java`.
    3. Refactor `MapRequestRepresentation.getDependencyExpression()` to extract the map construction logic into a private `getUnderlyingMapExpression()` method.
    4. Modify `MapFactoryCreationExpression` to use `TypeName.OBJECT` as fallback value type when the map type doesn't match standard provider/producer types, enabling more flexible type parameterization.
    5. Ensure all existing map request representations continue to work correctly with the refactored code structure.

32: /** Convenience methods for creating {@link CodeBlock}s. */
33: public final class CodeBlocks {
34:   /**
35:    * Joins {@link CodeBlock} instances in a manner suitable for use as method parameters (or
36:    * arguments).
37:    */
38:   public static Collector<CodeBlock, ?, CodeBlock> toParametersCodeBlock() {
39:     // TODO(ronshapiro,jakew): consider adding zero-width spaces to help line breaking when the
40:     // formatter is off. If not, inline this
41:     return CodeBlock.joining(", ");
42:   }
43: 
44:   /** Concatenates {@link CodeBlock} instances separated by newlines for readability. */
45:   public static Collector<CodeBlock, ?, CodeBlock> toConcatenatedCodeBlock() {
46:     return CodeBlock.joining("\n", "", "\n");
47:   }
48: 
49:   /** Returns a comma-separated version of {@code codeBlocks} as one unified {@link CodeBlock}. */
50:   public static CodeBlock makeParametersCodeBlock(Iterable<CodeBlock> codeBlocks) {
51:     return stream(codeBlocks.spliterator(), false).collect(toParametersCodeBlock());
52:   }
53: 
54:   /**
55:    * Returns a comma-separated {@link CodeBlock} using the name of every parameter in {@code
56:    * parameters}.
57:    */
58:   public static CodeBlock parameterNames(Iterable<ParameterSpec> parameters) {
59:     // TODO(ronshapiro): Add DaggerStreams.stream(Iterable)
60:     return stream(parameters.spliterator(), false)
61:         .map(p -> CodeBlock.of("$N", p))
62:         .collect(toParametersCodeBlock());
63:   }
64: 
65:   /**
66:    * Returns one unified {@link CodeBlock} which joins each item in {@code codeBlocks} with a
67:    * newline.
68:    */
69:   public static CodeBlock concat(Iterable<CodeBlock> codeBlocks) {
70:     return stream(codeBlocks.spliterator(), false).collect(toConcatenatedCodeBlock());
71:   }
72: 
73:   /**
74:    * Returns an anonymous {@link javax.inject.Provider} class with the single {@link
75:    * javax.inject.Provider#get()} method that returns the given {@code expression}.
76:    */
77:   public static CodeBlock anonymousProvider(Expression expression) {
78:     return anonymousProvider(
79:         expression.type().getTypeName(), CodeBlock.of("return $L;", expression.codeBlock()));
80:   }
81: 
82:   /**
83:    * Returns an anonymous {@link javax.inject.Provider} class with the single {@link
84:    * javax.inject.Provider#get()} method implemented by {@code body}.
85:    */
86:   public static CodeBlock anonymousProvider(TypeName providedType, CodeBlock body) {
87:     return CodeBlock.of(
88:         "$L",
89:         anonymousClassBuilder("")
90:             .superclass(daggerProviderOf(providedType))
91:             .addMethod(
92:                 methodBuilder("get")
93:                     .addAnnotation(Override.class)
94:                     .addModifiers(PUBLIC)
95:                     .returns(providedType)
96:                     .addCode(body)
97:                     .build())
98:             .build());
99:   }
100: 
101:   /** Returns {@code expression} cast to a type. */
102:   public static CodeBlock cast(CodeBlock expression, ClassName castTo) {
103:     return CodeBlock.of("($T) $L", castTo, expression);
104:   }
105: 
106:   /** Returns {@code expression} cast to a type. */
107:   public static CodeBlock cast(CodeBlock expression, Class<?> castTo) {
108:     return CodeBlock.of("($T) $L", castTo, expression);
109:   }
110: 
111:   public static CodeBlock type(XType type) {
112:     return CodeBlock.of("$T", type.getTypeName());
113:   }
114: 
115:   public static CodeBlock stringLiteral(String toWrap) {
116:     return CodeBlock.of("$S", toWrap);
117:   }

When a user annotates an Activity with `@AndroidEntryPoint` and specifies a base class (e.g., `@AndroidEntryPoint(BaseActivity.class)`), Hilt generates a subclass that overrides `onCreate` and `onDestroy` methods. These overridden methods are essential for Hilt's SavedStateHandle injection and cleanup functionality.

    However, if the user marks `onCreate` or `onDestroy` as `final` in the base Activity class, Hilt's generated subclass cannot override these methods, which leads to runtime failures or silent breakage of Hilt's state management. Currently, no warning or error is produced at compile time.

    **Goal:** Add a compile-time error message when the nearest override method for `onCreate` or `onDestroy` (found via `requireNearestOverrideMethod`) is marked as `final`. The error should be reported on the offending method element.

    **Implementation location:** This validation should be added in `ActivityGenerator.java`, specifically in the `onCreateComponentActivity()` and `onDestroyComponentActivity()` methods, right after fetching the `nearestOverrideMethod`.

## Environment Setup
Review the repository structure to understand the build system:
    - Check `WORKSPACE`, `BUILD`, and `build_defs.bzl` for Bazel build configuration
    - Check `javatests/BUILD` for test target definitions
    - Note that this is a Google repository using Bazel as the primary build system

## Implementation Plan
Steps to implement:
    1. In `ActivityGenerator.java`, import `javax.tools.Diagnostic` if not already imported.
    2. In `onCreateComponentActivity()`, after `requireNearestOverrideMethod(ActivityMethod.ON_CREATE, metadata)`, add a check:
       - If `nearestOverrideMethod.isFinal()`, call `env.getMessager().printMessage(Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR, "Do not mark onCreate as final in base Activity class, as Hilt needs to override it to inject SavedStateHandle.", nearestOverrideMethod)`.
    3. In `onDestroyComponentActivity()`, after `requireNearestOverrideMethod(ActivityMethod.ON_DESTROY, metadata)`, add a similar check:
       - If `nearestOverrideMethod.isFinal()`, call `env.getMessager().printMessage(Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR, "Do not mark onDestroy as final in base Activity class, as Hilt needs to override it to clean up SavedStateHandle.", nearestOverrideMethod)`.
    4. Add test cases in `ActivityGeneratorTest.java`:

       - Test with a final `onCreate` in immediate base class
       - Test with a final `onCreate` in a transitive (grandparent) base class
       - Test with a final `onDestroy` in a transitive (grandparent) base class

We need to add KSP (Kotlin Symbol Processing) support for the Dagger Android Proguard Processor. Currently, `ProguardProcessor.java` uses the standard Java annotation processing API (`AbstractProcessor`). The goal is to refactor this to use the XProcessing abstraction layer (Room Compiler Processing), which supports both Java (Javac) and Kotlin (KSP) processing environments.

    Specifically:
    1. Refactor the existing `ProguardProcessor.java` to extend `JavacBasicAnnotationProcessor` (from `androidx.room.compiler.processing.javac`).
    2. Create a new `KspProguardProcessor.java` that extends `KspBasicAnnotationProcessor` (from `androidx.room.compiler.processing.ksp`).
    3. Extract the actual proguard rule generation logic into a shared `ProguardProcessingStep.java` that extends the existing `BaseProcessingStep` class.
    4. Make `BaseProcessingStep` public and extract it into its own Bazel target so it can be shared between the proguard processor and the existing Android processor.
    5. Update the Bazel `BUILD` files to reflect these new dependencies and source files.

    The functionality must remain identical - generating proguard rules for Dagger Android projects:
    - `resources/META-INF/com.android.tools/proguard/dagger-android.pro`
    - `resources/META-INF/com.android.tools/r8/dagger-android.pro`
    - `resources/META-INF/proguard/dagger-android.pro`

## Environment Setup
Check the `WORKSPACE` file at the repository root to understand the Bazel workspace setup and external dependencies. The `java/dagger/android/internal/proguard/BUILD` and `java/dagger/android/processor/BUILD` files contain the Bazel build targets you'll need to modify. 35: /**

37:  * TypeNotPresentException} is thrown.

39: abstract class BaseProcessingStep implements XProcessingStep {
40:   @Override
41:   public final ImmutableSet<String> annotations() {
42:     return annotationClassNames().stream().map(ClassName::canonicalName).collect(toImmutableSet());
43:   }

45:   // Subclass must ensure all annotated targets are of valid type.
46:   @Override
47:   public ImmutableSet<XElement> process(
48:       XProcessingEnv env, Map<String, ? extends Set<? extends XElement>> elementsByAnnotation) {
49:     ImmutableSet.Builder<XElement> deferredElements = ImmutableSet.builder();
50:     inverse(elementsByAnnotation)
51:         .forEach(
52:             (element, annotations) -> {
53:               try {
54:                 process(element, annotations);
55:               } catch (TypeNotPresentException e) {
56:                 deferredElements.add(element);
57:               }
58:             });
59:     return deferredElements.build();
60:   }

67:    *     element}
68:    */
69:   protected abstract void process(XElement element, ImmutableSet<ClassName> annotations);

72:       Map<String, ? extends Set<? extends XElement>> elementsByAnnotation) {
73:     ImmutableMap<String, ClassName> annotationClassNames =
74:         annotationClassNames().stream()
75:             .collect(toImmutableMap(ClassName::canonicalName, className -> className));
76:     checkState(
77:         annotationClassNames.keySet().containsAll(elementsByAnnotation.keySet()),

79:         this.getClass().getCanonicalName(),
80:         difference(elementsByAnnotation.keySet(), annotationClassNames.keySet()));

82:     ImmutableSetMultimap.Builder<XElement, ClassName> builder = ImmutableSetMultimap.builder();
83:     elementsByAnnotation.forEach(
84:         (annotationName, elementSet) ->
85:             elementSet.forEach(
86:                 element -> builder.put(element, annotationClassNames.get(annotationName))));
87: 
88:     return ImmutableMap.copyOf(Maps.transformValues(builder.build().asMap(), ImmutableSet::copyOf));

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import base64, socket, threading, time, sys

LISTEN = ("127.0.0.1", 8899)
UPSTREAM = ("172.22.13.146", 3128)
AUTH = base64.b64encode(b"svc_proxy_nonrte_netgrp:jLNgeTuuCdbu9h9kesPaA4iEDrzHvXtR").decode()
LOG = open("/tmp/opencode/proxy.log", "a", buffering=1)

def log(*a):
    print(time.time(), *a, file=LOG)

def recv_headers(conn):
    data = b""
    while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data:
        chunk = conn.recv(4096)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
    return data

def relay(a, b, name):
    try:
        n = 0
        while True:
            data = a.recv(65536)
            if not data:
                break
            b.sendall(data)
            n += len(data)
        log("relay", name, "EOF after", n)
    except OSError as e:
        log("relay", name, "err", repr(e))
    finally:
        for s in (a, b):
            try:
                s.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

def handle(client):
    try:
        client.settimeout(30)
        req = recv_headers(client)
        if not req:
            client.close()
            return
        first = req.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0].decode("latin1", "replace")
        parts = first.split(" ")
        method = parts[0].upper()
        target = parts[1]
        log("req", method, target)
        if method == "CONNECT":
            up = socket.create_connection(UPSTREAM, timeout=30)
            up.sendall(("CONNECT %s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: %s\r\nProxy-Authorization: Basic %s\r\n\r\n" % (target, target, AUTH)).encode())
            resp = recv_headers(up)
            log("upstream CONNECT resp:", resp.split(b"\r\n",1)[0])
            if b" 200 " not in resp.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0]:
                up.close()
                client.close()
                return
            client.sendall(b"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n")
            t1 = threading.Thread(target=relay, args=(client, up, "c->u"), daemon=True)
            t2 = threading.Thread(target=relay, args=(up, client, "u->c"), daemon=True)
            t1.start(); t2.start()
            t1.join(); t2.join()
        else:
            up = socket.create_connection(UPSTREAM, timeout=30)
            lines = req.split(b"\r\n")
            out = lines[0] + b"\r\n"
            for h in lines[1:-1]:
                out += h + b"\r\n"
            out += b"Proxy-Authorization: Basic " + AUTH.encode() + b"\r\n"
            out += lines[-1]
            up.sendall(out)
            t = threading.Thread(target=relay, args=(up, client, "u->c"), daemon=True)
            relay(up, client, "u->c") if False else None
            t.start()
            relay(client, up, "c->u")
    except Exception as e:
        log("proxy error", repr(e))
        try:
            client.close()
        except OSError:
            pass

def main():
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    s.bind(LISTEN)
    s.listen(128)
    log("listening", LISTEN)
    while True:
        c, _ = s.accept()
        threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(c,), daemon=True).start()

92:         name,

110:     """Generates the files required for a maven artifact.
111: 
112:     This macro generates the following targets:
113:         * ":pom": The pom file for the given target and deps
114:         * ":<NAME>": The artifact file for the given target and deps
115:         * ":<NAME>-src": The sources jar file for the given target and deps
116:         * ":<NAME>-javadoc": The javadocs jar file for the given target and deps
117: 
118:     This macro also validates a few things. First, it validates that the
119:     given "target" is a maven artifact (i.e. the "tags" attribute contains
120:     "maven_coordinates=..."). Second, it calculates the list of transitive
121:     dependencies of the target that are not owned by another maven artifact,
122:     and validates that the given "deps" matches exactly.
123: 
124:     Args:
125:       name: The name associated with the various output targets.
126:       artifact_target: The target containing the maven_coordinates.
127:       artifact_name: The name of the maven artifact.
128:       artifact_coordinates: The coordinates of the maven artifact in the
129:                             form: "<group_id>:<artifact_id>:<version>"
130:       artifact_target_libs: The set of transitive libraries of the target.
131:       artifact_target_maven_deps: The required maven deps of the target.
132:       artifact_target_maven_deps_banned: The banned maven deps of the target.
133:       testonly: True if the jar should be testonly.
134:       packaging: The packaging of the maven artifact. E.g. "aar"
135:       pom_name: The name of the pom file (or "pom" if absent).
136:       javadoc_srcs: The srcs for the javadocs.
137:       javadoc_root_packages: The root packages for the javadocs.
138:       javadoc_exclude_packages: The packages to exclude from the javadocs.
139:       javadoc_android_api_level: The android api level for the javadocs.
140:       shaded_deps: The shaded deps for the jarjar.
141:       manifest: The AndroidManifest.xml to bundle in when packaing an 'aar'.
142:       lint_deps: The lint targets to be bundled in when packaging an 'aar'.
143:       proguard_specs: The proguard spec files to be bundled in when packaging an 'aar'
144:     """
145: 
146:     _validate_maven_deps(
147:         name = name + "-validation",
148:         testonly = 1,
149:         target = artifact_target,
150:         expected_artifact = artifact_coordinates,
151:         expected_libs = artifact_target_libs,
152:         expected_maven_deps = artifact_target_maven_deps,
153:         banned_maven_deps = artifact_target_maven_deps_banned,
154:     )
155: 
156:     shaded_deps = shaded_deps or []
157:     artifact_targets = [artifact_target] + (artifact_target_libs or [])
158:     lint_deps = lint_deps or []
159: 
160:     # META-INF resources files that can be combined by appending lines.
161:     merge_meta_inf_files = [

165:     artifact_id = artifact_coordinates.split(":")[1]

168:         testonly = testonly,
169:         artifact_id = artifact_id,
170:         artifact_name = artifact_name,
171:         packaging = packaging,
172:         targets = artifact_targets,
173:     )

175:     if (packaging == "aar"):

178:             testonly = testonly,
179:             jars = artifact_targets + shaded_deps,
180:             merge_meta_inf_files = merge_meta_inf_files,
181:         )
182:         if lint_deps:

184:             jarjar_library(

201:         else:

213:         native.genrule(
214:             name = name,
215:             srcs = [name + "-android-lib"],
216:             outs = [name + ".aar"],

224:             merge_meta_inf_files = merge_meta_inf_files,

229:         testonly = testonly,

259: def _validate_maven_deps_impl(ctx):
260:     """Validates the given Maven target and deps
261: 
262:     Validates that the given "target" is a maven artifact (i.e. the "tags"
263:     attribute contains "maven_coordinates=..."). Second, it calculates the

278:                 artifact,
279:             ),

281: 
282:     all_transitive_deps = target[MavenInfo].all_transitive_deps.to_list()
283:     maven_nearest_artifacts = target[MavenInfo].maven_nearest_artifacts.to_list()
284:     maven_transitive_deps = target[MavenInfo].maven_transitive_deps.to_list()
285: 
286:     expected_libs = [dep.label for dep in getattr(ctx.attr, "expected_libs", [])]
287:     actual_libs = [dep for dep in all_transitive_deps if dep not in maven_transitive_deps]
288:     _validate_list("artifact_target_libs", actual_libs, expected_libs)
289: 
290:     expected_maven_deps = [dep for dep in getattr(ctx.attr, "expected_maven_deps", [])]
291:     actual_maven_deps = [_strip_artifact_version(artifact) for artifact in maven_nearest_artifacts]
292:     _validate_list(
293:         "artifact_target_maven_deps",
294:         # Exclude shaded maven deps from this list since they're not actual dependencies.
295:         [dep for dep in actual_maven_deps if dep not in SHADED_MAVEN_DEPS],
296:         expected_maven_deps,
297:         ctx.attr.banned_maven_deps,
298:     )
299: 
300: def _validate_list(name, actual_list, expected_list, banned_list = []):
301:     missing = sorted(['"{}",'.format(x) for x in actual_list if x not in expected_list])
302:     if missing:
303:         fail("\t[Error]: Found missing {}: \n\t\t".format(name) + "\n\t\t".join(missing))
304: 
305:     extra = sorted(['"{}",'.format(x) for x in expected_list if x not in actual_list])
306:     if extra:

308: 
309:     banned = sorted(['"{}",'.format(x) for x in actual_list if x in banned_list])
310:     if banned:

1: #!/bin/bash
2: 
3: set -eu
4: 
5: # Builds and deploys the given artifacts to a configured maven goal.
6: # @param {string} library the library to deploy.
7: # @param {string} pomfile the pom file to deploy.
8: # @param {string} srcjar the sources jar of the library. This is an optional
9: # parameter, if provided then javadoc must also be provided.
10: # @param {string} javadoc the java doc jar of the library. This is an optional
11: # parameter, if provided then srcjar must also be provided.
12: # @param {string} module_name the JPMS module name to include in the jar. This
13: # is an optional parameter and can only be used with jar files.
14: deploy_library() {
15:   local shaded_rules=$1
16:   local library=$2
17:   local pomfile=$3
18:   local srcjar=$4
19:   local javadoc=$5
20:   local module_name=$6
21:   local mvn_goal=$7
22:   local version_name=$8
23:   shift 8
24:   local extra_maven_args=("$@")
25: 
26:   bazel build --define=pom_version="$version_name" $library $pomfile
27: 
28:   # Shade the library if shaded_rules exist
29:   if [[ ! -z "$shaded_rules" ]]; then
30:     bash $(dirname $0)/shade-library.sh \
31:       $(bazel_output_file $library) $shaded_rules
32:     # The output jar name is the same as the input library appended with -shaded
33:     library="${library%.*}-shaded.${library##*.}"
34:   fi
35: 
36:   # Validate that the classes in the library jar begin with expected prefixes.
37:   validate_jar $(bazel_output_file $library)
38: 
39:   # TODO(bcorso): Consider moving this into the "gen_maven_artifact" macro, this
40:   # requires having the version checked-in for the build system.
41:   add_tracking_version \
42:     $(bazel_output_file $library) \
43:     $(bazel_output_file $pomfile) \
44:     $version_name
45: 
46:   # TODO(bcorso): Consider moving this into the "gen_maven_artifact" macro once
47:   # all our targets are using gen_maven_artifact
48:   add_automatic_module_name_manifest_entry \
49:     $(bazel_output_file $library) \
50:     "${module_name}"
51: 
52:   if [ -n "$srcjar" ] && [ -n "$javadoc" ] ; then
53:     bazel build --define=pom_version="$version_name" \
54:       $srcjar $javadoc
55:     mvn $mvn_goal \
56:       -Dfile=$(bazel_output_file $library) \
57:       -Djavadoc=$(bazel_output_file $javadoc) \
58:       -DpomFile=$(bazel_output_file $pomfile) \
59:       -Dsources=$(bazel_output_file $srcjar) \
60:       "${extra_maven_args[@]:+${extra_maven_args[@]}}"
61:   else
62:     mvn $mvn_goal \
63:       -Dfile=$(bazel_output_file $library) \
64:       -DpomFile=$(bazel_output_file $pomfile) \
65:       "${extra_maven_args[@]:+${extra_maven_args[@]}}"
66:   fi
67: }
68: 
69: bazel_output_file() {
70:   local library=$1
71:   local output_file=bazel-bin/$library
72:   if [[ ! -e $output_file ]]; then
73:      output_file=bazel-genfiles/$library
74:   fi
75:   if [[ ! -e $output_file ]]; then
76:     echo "Could not find bazel output file for $library"
77:     exit 1
78:   fi
79:   echo -n $output_file
80: }
81: 
82: add_tracking_version() {
83:   local library=$1
84:   local pomfile=$2
85:   local version_name=$3
86:   local group_id=$(find_pom_value $pomfile "groupId")
87:   local artifact_id=$(find_pom_value $pomfile "artifactId")
88:   local temp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
89:   local version_file="META-INF/${group_id}_${artifact_id}.version"
90:   mkdir -p "$temp_dir/META-INF/"
91:   echo $version_name >> "$temp_dir/$version_file"
92:   if [[ $library =~ \.jar$ ]]; then
93:     jar uf $library -C $temp_dir $version_file
94:   elif [[ $library =~ \.aar$ ]]; then
95:     unzip $library classes.jar -d $temp_dir
96:     jar uf $temp_dir/classes.jar -C $temp_dir $version_file
97:     jar uf $library -C $temp_dir classes.jar
98:   else
99:     echo "Could not add tracking version file to $library"
100:     exit 1
101:   fi
102: }
103: 
104: validate_jar() {
105:   local library=$1
106:   if [[ $library == */gwt/libgwt.jar ]]; then
107:      python $(dirname $0)/validate-jar-entry-prefixes.py \
108:         $library "dagger/,META-INF/,javax/inject/"
109:   elif [[ $library == */java/dagger/hilt/android/artifact.aar ]]; then
110:      python $(dirname $0)/validate-jar-entry-prefixes.py \
111:         $library "dagger/,META-INF/,hilt_aggregated_deps/"
112:   else
113:      python $(dirname $0)/validate-jar-entry-prefixes.py \
114:         $library "dagger/,META-INF/"
115:   fi
116: }
117: 
118: add_automatic_module_name_manifest_entry() {
119:   local library=$1
120:   local module_name=$2
121:   if [ -n "$module_name" ] ; then
122:     if [[ $library =~ \.jar$ ]]; then
123:       local temp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
124:       echo "Automatic-Module-Name: ${module_name}" > $temp_dir/module_name_file
125:       # The "m" flag is specifically for adding manifest entries.
126:       jar ufm $library $temp_dir/module_name_file
127:     else
128:       echo "Could not add module name to $library"
129:       exit 1
130:     fi
131:   fi
132: }
133: 
134: find_pom_value() {
135:   local pomfile=$1
136:   local attribute=$2
137:   # Using Python here because `mvn help:evaluate` doesn't work with our gen pom
138:   # files since they don't include the aar packaging plugin.
139:   python $(dirname $0)/find_pom_value.py $pomfile $attribute
140: }
141: 
142: deploy_library "$@"

52:     srcs = getattr(ctx.rule.attr, "srcs", [])
